messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: routing-policy:capacity-tier anomalies detected for tenant=acme-corp — sudden increase in hosted assignment and error rate > 7% across requests. auto-page oncall

olivia: seeing it in the dashboard — latency up to 450ms P95 for acme-corp, errors are 503s from runtime router. paging now. @ryan can you join?

ryan: on it. i can repro a test trace that shows route decision flipping between 'dedicated:pool-a' and 'hosted:general' repeatedly. looks like policy eval returns both tiers as eligible and fallback pref chooses hosted.

meera: tagging platform rules owners — we recently shipped the "tier-blend" flag. did we change the eligibility predicate for isolation?

vikas: i rolled a policy patch last night to add region affinity for burst handling. patch id: config-2026-11-03-487. maybe related.

sam: customer success reporting real-time: acme-corp chat bot degraded, some users seeing timeouts. CS is adding customers to status page. emma is on the line with their SRE.

emma: acme SRE says they saw a spike starting ~2410000000, requests routed to hosted caused 10–15s tail latencies when the hosted pool hit GC. they're sensitive to model_variants — hosted picks a quantized variant which gives different tokenization behavior.

olivia: immediate mitigation idea: pin acme-corp to dedicated pool-a membership in routing table so policy won't evaluate fallback. can we make that change with a short rollback path?

ryan: we can add a temporary static mapping: write to route-db: `UPDATE tenant_routes SET pinned_pool='dedicated:pool-a' WHERE tenant='acme-corp';` then reload router config (rolls quickly). doing a dry-run now on staging.

deploy-bot: CONFIG APPLY (dry-run): config-2026-11-04-temp-pin-2410000000 by ryan -> OK on staging

ryan: applying to prod in 1 minute. will monitor.

(60s later)

olivia: ryan — status?

ryan: applied. router reload returned 0. traffic for acme-corp now consistently hitting dedicated:pool-a. errors down to 0.8% and P95 back to 80–90ms.

meera: great. can we also lock the policy engine to prevent automatic tier-fallthrough until we finish RCA? i want to avoid automatic flips during the investigation.

vikas: adding a guard: set `tier_fallthrough=false` in policy-runtime config. deploy in 30s.
\
deploy-bot: CONFIG APPLY: policy-runtime-tierguard-2410000030 by vikas -> completed

ryan: logging traces — found the root trigger: a corner-case in the variant compatibility check. when model_variant metadata lacks explicit `is_dedicated_compatible` flag, fallback comparator scored hosted variant slightly higher due to lower estimated cost. effectively the comparator didn't enforce tenant isolation precedence.

olivia: so it's not a capacity shortage, it's policy scoring ordering that allowed hosted to be chosen even though dedicated was preferred. that explains the tokenization mismatch and the customer impact.

emergency action items:
- pin tenant to dedicated (done)
- disable automatic fallthrough (done)
- backfill variant metadata to mark dedicated-only variants (in progress)
- write test to fail on missing compatibility flag (in-progress)

sam: advising acme-corp CS contact: we've routed them back to dedicated, impact window ~2m, no data exfil, varied responses only due to variant mismatch. asking for confirmation they see normal behavior.

emma: acme says their bot latency returned to normal and tokenization drift resolved. will keep monitoring.

ryan: for RCA: reproducer attached — example trace below (private):
```
trace: tenant=acme-corp request_id=req-2410000055
policy_eval: candidates=[dedicated:pool-a|variant=redwood-v1, hosted:general|variant=redwood-v1-quant]
score(dedicated)=0.91, score(hosted)=0.93 -> chosen=hosted
compatibility: dedicated:missing_flag, hosted:inferred_ok
```

meera: action: we need a safe typing rule so missing flags are treated as not-compatible for isolation-critical tenants. otherwise comparator can prefer lower-cost hosted variants.

vikas: agreed. creating follow-up JIRA: CAP-3129 "treat missing compatibility as incompatible for tenant-isolation" and CAP-3130 "add policy unit tests for tier precedence".

olivia: hands-off to post-incident oncall: @ryan will own the initial RCA doc and deploy metadata backfills, @meera and @vikas to own policy test & config release, @sam & @emma to handle customer comms. I'll keep this thread pinned until postmortem is filed.

ryan: filing notes now. tentative timeline: full backfill + tests by EOD, config change to re-enable fallthrough with safeguard in 24h.

deploy-bot: NOTE: scheduled config change to re-enable fallthrough with extra guard -> schedule id sched-2410000450 created

olivia: final status: mitigation successful, customer impact limited, ongoing work to harden comparator and metadata hygiene. will escalate to on-call review meeting at 10:30.

sam: adding follow-up: run query to list tenants with missing compatibility flags and high isolation requirement, get a prioritized list for backfill.

emma: cc'ing account execs for acme-corp with summary and timeline.

olivia: thanks all — great rapid response. next: postmortem draft + link to RCA artifacts (traces, config diffs) in #postmortems.

(END)
